title: Heuristic alias generator for function<->tool interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a runtime and tooling component that automatically proposes and optionally applies alias mappings between legacy function names (internal function APIs) and OpenAI-style tool names. Goal: reduce friction for customers migrating to the OpenAI-style tool calling surface while keeping deterministic fallbacks and an auditable mapping history.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can apply a mapping table to incoming tool/function invocation requests with <=1ms median added latency
Alias generator suggests mappings for 95% of observed legacy function names in our telemetry samples with a confidence score
Mappings are reversible and produce an audit trail accessible in Console (per-tenant)
Conflict resolution policy implemented: deterministic precedence rules + human review queue
E2E tests cover streaming invocations that use an aliased mapping and ensure streaming semantics preserved
Feature can be enabled per-customer and toggled in Dedicated/Private deployments via config
discussion: We currently see frequent customer friction where tools registered with OpenAI-style metadata can't be invoked by older clients still emitting legacy function names. Manual mapping is error-prone. Proposal: a heuristic alias generator that uses deterministic name normalization (snake/camel/kebab normalization, punctuation stripping, semantic tokenization) followed by a lightweight ML suggestion layer that offers candidate aliases when deterministic rules are ambiguous. Generated aliases are stored in a per-tenant mapping table with provenance (generator version, heuristics used, confidence). Runtime applies mapping with a confidence threshold and falls back to legacy resolution if ambiguity is high.
decisions: (1) Start with deterministic rule set first, add ML suggestion as opt-in during rollout. (2) Store mappings as first-class objects with created_by: {auto|engineer}, source: {heuristic|human}, and timestamp. (3) Mapping application is a non-destructive layer: we never modify original request fields and always attach invocation provenance headers for debugging. (4) Console will show suggested aliases in the Functions & Tools page and provide a one-click approve + apply flow.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect mappings could route sensitive calls incorrectly or break authorization. Mitigation: require admin approval before auto-apply for tenants with 'strict-compat' flag; provide a dry-run mode that logs would-be mappings; run canary on 10% of traffic initially. Risk: increased latency. Mitigation: keep mapping lookup O(1) via hash maps and cache recent resolutions; measure latency impact with microbenchmarks.
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization rules, integration tests for runtime lookup, load tests to validate latency under steady-state QPS, and cross-tenant isolation tests. Add golden-mapping fixtures to CI. Add fuzz tests for edge-case punctuation and unicode names.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfood (redwood engineers) with auto-suggest only. Phase 2: opt-in beta customers with dry-run logging and console suggestions. Phase 3: enable auto-apply for non-strict tenants with canary at 10% then 50% then 100%. Provide rollback knob and mapping revocation API.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track alias_suggested_count, alias_auto_applied_count, alias_conflict_rate, alias_false_positive_rate (via post-mortem sampling), avg_added_latency_ms, customer_error_rate_change. Surface these in Console per-tenant.
notes: Design doc contains example heuristics: strip common verbs (get/fetch/fetcher), map 'create_user' -> 'user.create', handle namespace tokens like 'billing.invoice.generate' heuristically. Preference order: exact match > deterministic normalized match > admin-approved alias > ML-suggested alias. If multiple candidates tie, we enqueue for human review and fail open only for non-strict tenants.
next_steps: (1) Finalize normalization rule set (Aisha). (2) Prototype MR for runtime lookup module (Marco). (3) Console mockups for alias review UI (Jin). (4) Security review kickoff and threat model (Ruth).
